title: Co-writing credits and patching lyrics
summary: Matassa explains his name on Pontchartrain Music writers' credits: he contributed lyrics and patched weak ones, and says writers hate being told to rewrite.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: One question I wanted to ask, I was looking at some of these records. And it says Pontchartrain Music Corporation, which I'm sure is you, and this is affiliated with BMI.

But under writer's credits, it's got Mack Rabinac. This is the Chuck Carbo song, Promise. Mack Rabinac. I guess it's Seth David. Yeah. And then it's got Matassa. It's got you. Yeah. Did you, were you a writer? What was it? I'll work on it.
You've got to know all these things have gone in the studio.
Somebody come in with an idea and it will change a feather and a wishbone into a chicken.

Oh, okay. So, yeah, because you're on the flip side is Be My Girl by, you know, Chuck Carbo, and again, Rabinac, David, and Matassa. Okay. So, you were a writer, so you were. Well, I was, you know, I was a part of the conspiracy. Oh, okay. So, it was more, not so much as a writer or contributing a lyric.
Mostly lyrics, actually. But, so you did contribute? Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Yeah. And also patched lyrics.
Mm-hmm. Where people's choice of words wasn't too good.

In fact, the toughest thing, generically speaking, the toughest thing I found in the past, and I suppose it's still a problem today, was that you tell a writer to rewrite something. Right. And they'd be offended. They'd be hurt.

You know, oh, no, no. And I try to tell them that, well, if writing is going to be a craft, you know, then you're going to have to look at it as something that you use, you learn to use tools. Right. Sure. And you apply those tools to the thing you're working on, and those tools tell you from time to time, this word doesn't work as well. Right.
And you try other words or other phrases, or you move verse two to verse three, and verse three back to verse four.
Right. I mean, yeah, just using a good common sense. Yeah. And the idea that it's a developmental rather than an inspirational experience. Yeah, right.
You know? That was a tough sell. Still is. Yeah. Amateur writers in general, it's like asking them to stab their child. It's just, you don't want to do it.
